_comment: Which cloud provides each capability, per scope. The engine ships brand- AND vendor-neutral: an organization picks its provider here, and nothing above this file knows which one it got. Google is IMPLEMENTED; Azure and AWS are DECLARED AND UNIMPLEMENTED — they refuse loudly rather than silently falling back, because a capability that quietly degrades to nothing is how a control plane ends up believing it tokenized something it did not.

_fields.status: implemented = wired and callable · stub = the shape exists, the calls do not · unsupported = no path, refuse
_fields.egress: the domains this provider needs. Runners are default-deny; adding a provider is an EXPLICIT egress decision, not a consequence of selecting it
_fields.processor: the legal relationship required before tenant data may flow. ADR 0010 rejects any processor without one for tenant work
_fields.notes: what a reader needs before choosing it

_choosing: Set `default_provider`, or override per capability. A scope may override both — a tenant whose contract forbids one vendor is a scope-level setting, not a fork.

transcription.why: Tenant call transcripts with SPEAKER IDENTITY, not just diarization — see ADR 0015.

google.service: Google Meet built-in transcription -> Drive -> drive-sync -> scrubber
google.identity: real participant identity from the Workspace directory
google.notes: Requires a Workspace tier that includes transcription — UNVERIFIED, see ADR 0015. Adds no new processor if Workspace is already in place.

azure.service: Azure AI Speech batch transcription + speaker diarization
azure.identity: acoustic diarization only — speakers are clusters, not people, unless Teams supplies identity
azure.processor: Azure DPA / EU Data Boundary if applicable
azure.notes: Not built. Teams transcription is the identity-bearing equivalent of the Google path; raw Speech services are not.

aws.notes: Not built. No native meeting-identity source, so the department-grouping requirement in ADR 0015 would need solving separately.

object_store.why: Where an engagement's artifacts land before the scrubber sees them.

google.service: Google Drive (already wired by the drive-sync workflow)
google.notes: drive-sync exists and has NEVER RUN — it needs OAuth. Treat as untested.

secrets.why: ADR 0009 names managed secrets as a requirement of the always-on deployment; today it is a gitignored .env.

google.notes: Not built. .env is the current mechanism and is honest about being one.

dlp.why: The scrubber's detection backend. Heuristics ship in-repo; a cloud DLP is the optional upgrade named in DETECTION-BACKENDS.md.

google.notes: Documented in GSUITE-GCP.md, not wired. The built-in heuristic detector is the default and the fail-safe.

model.why: Where the router's tiers actually execute. Distinct from the CLI runners, which are their own auth path.

google.service: Vertex AI (enterprise terms) — as opposed to the AI Studio free tier the gemini-runner uses today
google.notes: THE LIVE GAP: gemini-runner authenticates with a free AI Studio key, not a Workspace or Vertex credential. Same vendor, different terms. See ADR 0015.
